comment: Corpus items are byte-exact slices of real transcripts from THIS repo's own Claude Code sessions, stored under ~/.claude/projects/<mangled-repo-path>/<session>.jsonl. Not committed (see README): only session id + line/byte range, so a run is reproducible on this machine without carrying raw transcript content into git. line numbers are 1-indexed and inclusive; byte ranges are the exact [from,to) slice runner.go reads and are what actually gets fed to internal/transcript.Read — regenerate them with scripts/offsets.py if the source files ever change.

items.name: engineering
items.description: Fixing OPEN-ITEMS one by one; init runs against real opencode and immediately turns up a real bug (claims it wrote four docs, only created two). Concrete problem, concrete fix, no product discussion.

items.name: product
items.description: Design conversation about what scribe is at its core and what should trigger a run. No code touched, but real product decisions get made (transcript-compiler framing, Stop-hook-per-reply as the trigger) — the kind of thing DECISIONS.md/PROJECT.md should pick up and CHANGELOG/JOURNAL should not.

items.name: reversal
items.description: Assistant claims PRs are stacked, user pushes back, assistant explicitly self-corrects ('Correction: they aren't stacked. They're siblings... I described them as stacked earlier; that was wrong.'). Tests whether the writer records the correction honestly instead of just the final state.

items.name: deadend
items.description: 'Files changed' as the unit of what a session did gets proposed, then explicitly scrapped by the user for not covering discussion-only sessions ('scrap files changed as the point'), in favor of tracking problems/decisions instead. Tests whether the writer notices an idea was raised and dropped, and records why, instead of writing it up as if it shipped.
